acceptance_signals: Validation command strings remain the admitted task contract and their original text continues to define persisted command identity.

Windows validation uses an explicit powershell.exe argv with NoLogo, NoProfile, NonInteractive, and UTF-16LE EncodedCommand; source quoting survives and native or PowerShell failure status is propagated.
POSIX validation uses an explicit /bin/sh -c argv, and subprocess execution no longer uses shell=True.

Fixture tests cover Windows environment assignment, quoting, success, nonzero native exit propagation, PowerShell failure, POSIX success and failure, unsupported platform or unavailable interpreter fail-closed behavior, and exact platform argv construction.
Timeout, stop-after-first-failure, transient raw output, persisted output digests, authority denial, and snapshot mutation detection remain unchanged.
The durable fresh-evidence specification and user workflow documentation state the platform shell and trust boundary without implying sandboxing.

Focused and full unit tests, the exact task check, repository check, and git diff check complete with all deterministic failures resolved except any separately disclosed pre-existing excluded-path completion limitation.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-ecb7aa64b869471e8dbe3a98e839930e and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control.

requirement.summary: Replace implicit shell=True validation execution with an explicit platform-native runner while preserving the existing string command contract, evidence identity, privacy boundary, timeout, first-failure behavior, and snapshot freshness semantics. On Windows, execute an encoded noninteractive Windows PowerShell script and propagate native or PowerShell failure status; on POSIX, execute through /bin/sh -c. This task does not change excluded-path completion semantics.

items: PowerShell wrapping or encoding could alter quoting or exit-code behavior if not tested with real Windows subprocesses.
Platform dispatch could fail on unsupported hosts or hosts missing the declared interpreter; the runner must fail closed with a bounded error.
Pre-existing excluded changed paths may still prevent formal completion even when the shell repair itself passes; this task must not silently broaden scope or change that separate policy.
Reviewed assumption: The existing validation_commands array of strings is intentionally retained as platform-native shell source rather than migrated to structured argv metadata.
Reviewed assumption: Supported Windows environments provide powershell.exe and supported POSIX environments provide /bin/sh.
Reviewed assumption: The caller launches AgentGov with any required process environment such as PYTHONPATH; task validation commands need not mutate that environment themselves.
Reviewed unknown: Whether excluded changed paths should be ignored by completion is a separate unresolved requirement and is outside this task.
Reviewed unknown: Published-package and external consumer rollout are not authorized by this development-source repair.

title: Make declared validation execution shell-aware and deterministic
